suggestions.title: Sitemap and head hygiene that a crawler can verify, not imitate
suggestions.what: Three mechanical edits, no copy involved: give every listed page a <lastmod> taken from its own last git commit date; drop 404.html and the meta-refresh stubs from the URL set the sitemap publishes; and make the head block identical in shape across the six reader surfaces (title, description, canonical, og:title/og:description/og:image, one JSON-LD block). Measured today: 101 sitemap URLs with 0 lastmod, canonical on 102 of 136 pages, og:image and JSON-LD on 11 of 136 (all of read/).
suggestions.why: A polished site and an audit site look the same to a crawler; the difference is in the head. Google's sitemap guidance is explicit that lastmod counts only when it is 'consistently and verifiably' accurate, so a build-time date would be worse than none and a git date is the verifiable one. Google also ignores priority and changefreq, so nothing is lost by not adding them.

compliance.text: Google: 'Include the URLs in your sitemap that you want to see in Google's search results.' and 'Google uses the <lastmod> value if it's consistently and verifiably (for example by comparing to the last modification of the page) accurate.' and 'Google ignores <priority> and <changefreq> values.'

Google: 'Identical or similar descriptions on every page of a site aren't helpful when individual pages appear in search results' - which the register's measured title and description audit already satisfies (0 missing, 0 under 60 characters, one duplicate on the redirect stubs).

suggestions.blocker: Two generators write sitemap.xml (scripts/build_sitemap.py and tools/build_site.py), so the fix is one owner, not one edit - see flag G0B2-F-06.

suggestions.title: One social card per reader surface, drawn only from this site's own artwork
suggestions.what: Publish a 1200x630 preview card per reader surface and reference it from og:image and twitter:card on every reader page. The card is typographic: the guide's question, the site name, and the 'checked against the listing' date - the same three things the page leads with. No product photography, no Amazon imagery, no generated picture of a product.
suggestions.why: A shared link is the only marketing channel that costs nothing here, and it currently shows a title and nothing else on five of the six surfaces (measured: og:image on 11 of 136 pages, all read/). A typographic card also happens to be the honest one: the site has no right to display Amazon's images, and it has not tested a single product, so an invented 'lifestyle' shot would be the exact tell the owner asked to remove.

compliance.text: Program Content (which includes the listing's images and text) may not be copied onto the Site; the site's own gate enforces it - verify_site V6 fails any whose src is an Amazon asset or CDN host.

S-18 in the owner's own list ('add real product photography, and never generated or copied photography') is recorded as 'Needs a decision first' - so this suggestion ships without photography, and keeps the photography question open rather than answering it with a generated image.

suggestions.title: Aggregate-only click measurement, so the reporting half of the design is legal to build
suggestions.what: A per-page outbound click counter (static, first-party, no cookies, no user identifier) next to the existing dated register, and a rule written into the campaign ledger: sub-tags and Associates reporting are never associated with a specific end user. Segment by page, guide and date - never by visitor.
suggestions.why: This is the gate that decides how far the 'conversion-ready' redesign can go. The owner brief asks for click and conversion measurement; Amazon's clause says a site may not dynamically assign sub-tags to users or tie program reporting to an individual. Aggregate counts are allowed, per-person attribution is not, and a marketing redesign that quietly adds the second one is worse than no redesign. Measured today against that layer: its store is per UTC day, per event, per page path, per link host and token - a count and nothing else, no IP address, user agent, referrer or client-supplied date - which is what the aggregate rule asks for, and it stays compatible with Participation Requirements 2(b)'s ban on tying program reporting to a specific end user (PF-58).

compliance.text: 'Under no circumstances may you associate any sub-tag, other ID or reporting provided in connection with the Associates Program with a specific end user of your Site (e.g., you may not dynamically assign sub-tags to users as they arrive on your Site for purposes of monitoring such users' behavior).' - read verbatim 2026-11-17.
'You will not artificially generate clicks or impressions on your Site or create Sessions on an Amazon Site, whether by way of a robot or software program or otherwise.' - PF-33.

suggestions.blocker: Nothing to build, in fact: a privacy-preserving collector and an off-by-default counter already exist in this repository (tools/analytics_endpoint.py, assets/measure.js, site/measure.html, built by session 38650305 / ded63349, self-test passing, counting OFF until an endpoint_url is set). What waits is owner-side: host the collector, and confirm or replace the five event names it proposes. No counter, no analytics script and no event vocabulary is added by this proposal.

suggestions.title: Make 'checked date + source' the visual signature instead of urgency
suggestions.what: One badge style, used everywhere: 'Checked 17 Nov 2026 - from the listing'. It sits on every product card, guide header and comparison row, links to the dated source register row, and ages visibly. Paired with this, the layout can afford to be confident and quiet: one serif display face for the questions, a wide measure, generous whitespace, no countdown, no 'deal ends', no animated carousel.
suggestions.why: This is the cheapest available answer to 'it must not read like AI slop'. Generic affiliate pages buy attention with urgency and manufactured specificity ('limited time!', 'our top pick'). This site's real asset is the opposite: every claim has a date and a source, which is also the only kind of specificity the rules leave available while there is no API feed and no first-hand testing. The badge is marketing because it is a promise a competitor cannot copy without doing the work.

compliance.text: 'You must remove from your Site any links and related references to limited time promotions as soon as that promotion on the relevant Amazon Site ends.' - read verbatim 2026-11-17, so a countdown widget needs an owner and a dated check before it can exist.
'You can't talk about your experience with a product you haven't tried.' - so the badge dates the source, never the reviewer.

questions.question: What is the Associates tag (tracking ID) to use on every Special Link?

questions.question: Are the three destination listings the products that were intended?
questions.what_we_know: Each submitted short link opens a specific live listing: B0CDY277D3, B09B7SB46R, B08DKYBTPH. The mapping is stable across captures by three sessions, but no official source ties the links to the intended products.

questions.what_we_know: The site already publishes a verification protocol and a flagged-for-review process.
questions.what_we_dont_know: The owner's cadence and named reviewer.
questions.why_it_matters: The human-review gate (SUG-03) is the main defence against the AI-slop feel; without a real reviewer it is cosmetic.

questions.question: Which reader layer becomes the canonical shop the owner shows buyers — site/, read/, or marketing/?
questions.what_we_know: Measured on 2026-11-17, not estimated: six reader surfaces exist - site/ (20 pages, measured on the merged tree), read/ (11), shop/ (11), marketing/ (7), guides/ (5), articles/ (5) - plus 25 root register pages, and the root page is now a publication front page. questions.why_it_matters: It changes one collect() list in scripts/build_sitemap.py plus a noindex rule in the generator - and it is the difference between 'one site to index' and 136 pages of mixed intent competing with their own guides.

questions.what_we_know: The clause read verbatim today forbids associating any sub-tag or program reporting with a specific end user (PF-59, S80). The site today records no clicks at all; the ledger is empty by design and every column names its required source.

Note for whoever answers this: the in-tree collector (tools/analytics_endpoint.py) is already aggregate-only and already off until an endpoint is set, so the answer is a hosting decision plus a yes/no on the five proposed event names, not a design question.

paths.name: Shopfront first, lab underneath
paths.thesis: A buyer decides in seconds at the shelf; the verification machinery stays one click away but never above the fold. The site stops reading like an audit by changing what is FIRST, not by adding decoration.
steps: Open site/index.html with the three-question chooser already built for this purpose (decision D-23 in the brief's list) — move it above the product cards; every answer deep-links to the comparison row it affects.

Give each product card a 'fits you if / not for you if' pair of lines generated ONLY from quoted listing features — the generator already blocks any other sentence (i2_gate G6/G7), so catchiness comes from layout, not from invented claims.
Below the cards, one strip: 'New this week from the guides desk' fed by the same register that now backs feed.xml; dated, never ranked.
Disclosure strip stays exactly where it is (above the fold, every page, repeated in the footer) — the polish must not move it, and the lint enforces that it wasn't.
Keep every dashboard surface (flagged, sources, verification, decision pages) reachable from the footer and the single nav group — already true; do not add nav items, fold new ones in.
paths.resolves: The look half of SUG-01 and SUG-04; the brief's 'lead with the products' rule; consistent with S-17/S-19 as implemented.
paths.effort: One generator pass over site/ home + front-door region; no new data files; every gate already exists.
paths.risk: Low. Worst case the page reverts on a rebuild — the same self-healing pattern the feed uses now covers it.
paths.do_not: No prices, no star ratings, no review counts, no 'bestseller' badge until the API feed exists (2(b)/6(t)); no 'trending' without a dated first-party snapshot (the evidence rule already adopted).

paths.name: Magazine desk: voice and cadence carry it
paths.thesis: The fastest way to stop reading like AI slop is a real editorial calendar with a named human gate: one dated question per week, an author byline, and a 'what changed since last read' box that only a desk that re-reads sources can write.
steps: Adopt the cadence in the review below: one guide per week, each new guide lands in sitemap + feed automatically because both are register-driven now.

Add a byline block ('Field Notes desk — reviewed by: <name>') once Q5 names the human reviewer; until then the reviewed_by line stating 'no human editor' stays (it is already there; polishing would mean removing it, which we will not do).
Two held topics become publishable ONLY with owner inputs: testing/first-hand use (Q6) or the API for figures (Q4); do not write them softer to ship them.
Keep titles question-shaped like the five live guides; the brief's own suggested titles are all published — the next topic should come from the D8 query report, not from instinct.
paths.resolves: SUG-02, SUG-03, SUG-10, S-07's cadence half, and the 'catchy trendy articles' ask — honestly: catchy within what the compliance gates allow.
paths.effort: Editorial continuity, not code: the machinery (register, lint, feed, sitemap) already carries a weekly page in under an hour.
paths.risk: Cadence decays without a named owner; the site must never ship a 'latest' widget that goes stale — the register dates everything for exactly this reason.
paths.do_not: No synthetic social proof, no 'most popular', no AI-author persona names.

paths.name: Consolidate, then decorate
paths.thesis: Three parallel reader layers (site/, read/, marketing/) say near-the-same things about the same three products in three voices. That is both the strongest 'generated' tell and the reason search cannot pick a winner. One canonical layer fixes the findability ask and most of the slop feel at once.
steps: Owner answers Q12 (choose the canonical layer). Recommendation recorded here: promote site/ (the layer with the working house lint and release gates) and mark read/ + marketing/ as companion research with cross-links, not duplicates.
One navigation, one feed (the new feed.xml grows to cover the layer chosen), one sitemap (already covers everything; consolidation is a link-and-banner change, not a build change).
Fold the surviving extras (photography once S-18 decides, any API data once Q4 clears) into the chosen layer only, so polish is not written three times.
paths.resolves: 'One site to index and a reason to rank it' from the brief; Z14-F-04; the duplication note; most of Q7's brand-open residue.
paths.effort: Small edits, but touches the most shared files in the repo — must be ONE integration session (per the coordination protocol), not three parallel ones.
paths.risk: Link churn: internal cross-links and the sitemap shift. The gates in scripts/ catch every broken one before push.
paths.do_not: Do not delete the losing layers (history rule: archives stay); do not hand-merge the three feeds of copy into one without re-running every gate on the result.

That is the strongest 'generated' tell on the site and the reason search cannot pick a winner; it is also why the design prompt below names a layer as its first input rather than assuming one.

prompt.intro: Held as a file so a design session can be handed one document instead of a chat: DESIGN_PROMPT.md at the repository root. It is assembled only from decisions already recorded in this repository plus the official pages read today, and it is a draft until a path (DP-A/B/C) and Q12/Q13 are answered.
feel: Reads as a shop that happens to keep receipts, not as a lab that occasionally sells things: the product and the question are above the fold, the verification is one click away and never above it.
Specific instead of enthusiastic: a dated 'checked' chip, a source link on every claim row, and no adjective that a listing page cannot support.
One voice per surface. Six brands is the current state and the cost of not answering Q12; the prompt assumes one is chosen and the others become companion sections with cross-links, not duplicates.

rails.rule: 'You must clearly and prominently state ... As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases.' - Operating Agreement Section 5; a breach of Section 5 'will be deemed a material breach'.
rails.meaning: The strip under the masthead and the footer repeat stay. A redesign may restyle the strip; it may not move, shrink or 'clean' it off the fold, and the lint that checks placement must stay green.

rails.rail: No price, availability, rating or review count
rails.rule: 'your Site may only show prices and availability if: (a) we serve the link in which that price and availability data are displayed, or (b) you obtain Product pricing and availability data via Creators API or PA API'; customer reviews and star ratings only if obtained through the API.
rails.meaning: No price chip, no strikethrough was-price, no star row, no '4.7 from 12,000 reviews' in any card, table, meta description or preview image. The layout has to look confident without them - which is the design problem, and the reason the dated-source chip is the hero element.

rails.rail: No countdown, 'deal ends', or promo badge
rails.rule: 'You must remove from your Site any links and related references to limited time promotions as soon as that promotion on the relevant Amazon Site ends.'
rails.meaning: Urgency modules are not forbidden by policy, they are forbidden by maintenance: they need a named owner and a dated re-check before they can exist. Until one exists, none ships.

rails.rail: Comparison tables compare features, not prices
rails.rule: Displaying prices 'in any comparison format ... together with prices for the same or similar products offered through any web site ... other than an Amazon Site' obliges the site to show Amazon's lowest new (and, when provided, lowest used) price.
rails.meaning: The comparison stays capacity/dimensions/claims-based. Adding a price column is not a copy edit, it is a licence to publish a whole table you cannot populate.

rails.rail: Links stay direct, visible and un-bookmarked
rails.rule: 'You must not encourage customers to bookmark your Special Links. All Special Links must be accessed directly from your Site.' Plus: no link shortening or presentation 'in a manner that makes it unclear that you are linking to an Amazon Site'.
rails.meaning: No 'save for later' affordance on a buy link, no intermediate interstitial, no cute 'get it now' button that hides the destination. The button text names Amazon; rel=sponsored stays (Google's own guidance for paid placements).

rails.rule: 'Under no circumstances may you associate any sub-tag, other ID or reporting provided in connection with the Associates Program with a specific end user of your Site (e.g., you may not dynamically assign sub-tags to users as they arrive on your Site for purposes of monitoring such users' behavior).'
rails.meaning: A per-page click counter and dated campaign rows are buildable; per-visitor journeys, personalised sub-tags and user-level joins to Associates reports are not. This is the constraint the brief's Priority 4 has to be shaped around.

rails.rail: A product-list page needs its own reason to exist
rails.rule: 'When linking to pages with Product lists you must have additional original content on your Site that is relevant to the Special Link.' Enrolment-side: 'Your Site(s) must contain original content ... Original content utilizing third-party materials must contain significant commentary, analysis, or transformation'.
rails.meaning: A grid of cards is not a landing page. Every surface that links to a listing carries analysis the listing does not have - which is exactly what the guides, the capacity maths and the counter-space piece are for.

rails.rail: No Amazon imagery, and no invented product imagery
rails.rule: Program Content belongs to Amazon and may not be copied onto the Site; this repository's own gate (verify_site V6) fails any whose src is an Amazon asset or CDN host.
rails.meaning: Illustrations are this site's own artwork only. Real product photography is S-18, still 'needs a decision' - so a redesign ships with typographic and diagrammatic imagery, not with a generated photo of an air fryer.

sections.name: Masthead and disclosure
sections.spec: Wordmark, one-line promise, six-item nav maximum. Disclosure strip immediately under it, full width, contrast-checked, repeated in the footer. Nothing in the redesign changes its position; the lint fails the build if it moves.

sections.name: Front page shelf
sections.spec: Five product cards (three air fryers, two thermometers labelled as outside the air-fryer guides until Q16 answers). Each card: listing title as served, the observed ASIN with its date, a 'fits you if / not for you if' pair generated only from quoted listing features, and one sponsored button. The three-question chooser sits above the shelf, not below it.

sections.name: Guides desk
sections.spec: Question-shaped titles, dated byline block stating plainly that the desk is an agent desk until a human reviewer is named (Q5), and a 'what changed since this was written' line that only a re-read can produce. One guide a week, each one landing in the register, feed and sitemap by construction.

sections.name: Comparison
sections.spec: Feature rows with a source cell per row; sticky mobile bar; no price column (see the rails). The counter-space analysis - capacity per centimetre of counter depth - is the section a buyer cannot get from a listing, so it leads, not the spec grid.

sections.name: Imagery
sections.spec: Own artwork: diagrams for capacity and clearance, typographic social cards, one favicon set. No stock, no Amazon assets, no generated product photos.

sections.name: Head block
sections.spec: Per page: unique title, unique description that says what the page checked (no price), canonical, og:title/og:description/og:image, one JSON-LD block (Article/BreadcrumbList). No FAQPage: Google removed that rich-result documentation in June 2026, so the guides stand on reader value.

sections.name: Governance footer
sections.spec: Every dashboard, source register, verification log and flagged page stays reachable from the footer in one group. Readers never see the audit; auditors never lose the page.

avoid: 'Best', 'top-rated', 'most popular', 'trending' - not one of them, without a dated first-party snapshot behind it, and there is no snapshot endpoint to produce one.
Any number that is not on a page we opened: ratings, review counts, sales, 'bought in past month', conversion rates.
A persona byline ('our team of expert testers') - the FTC rule is that you cannot talk about a product you have not tried, and an invented expert is worse than an honest agent desk.
Price-comparison framing, countdowns, 'almost gone' stock language, exit pop-ups.
A second landing page for the same products. Until Q12 is answered the site already has six; a redesign must reduce that, not add to it.

decision_readiness.unblocks: The one thing a listing cannot tell a reader - what the appliance is like to live with - as a real, allowed content lane.
decision_readiness.default: S-06 stays 'not adopted'; guides keep the no-invented-experience rule the lint enforces.

decision_readiness.answer: Aggregate-only per-page counts accepted? Self-hosted endpoint wanted, given Pages serves static files only?

decision_readiness.unblocks: The click counter and the campaign ledger's measurement half.
decision_readiness.default: Empty ledger, dated, with columns naming the authorized first-party source each value must come from.
decision_readiness.where: COORDINATION.md decision log; the ledger schema in campaigns.html.

paths_status.changed: Still the cheapest look-for-the-money path, and now it has its rails written down.
paths_status.cost_now: Unchanged: one generator pass over the site/ home and front-door region, now twenty pages rather than eighteen. Compatible with any Q12 answer except 'fold everything into shop/'.

paths_status.changed: The cadence machinery is shipped (register-driven feed and sitemap); what it lacks is a name.
paths_status.cost_now: Editorial continuity, not code. Blocked half on Q5 (reviewer) and Q6 (testing lane), not on tooling.

paths_status.changed: Recosted on the merged tree: not 'small edits' but a six-surface decision - 59 reader pages across five brands, 136 pages in the published tree, with only read/ carrying a head block.
paths_status.cost_now: One integration session, banners and cross-links first, no deletions. This is now the highest-value path, because it is the only one that improves both the slop signal and the indexing story at once.

review_2026_11_17b.measurement: Findability numbers measured on the merged tree 2026-11-17, for the owner to sanity-check any later claim of 'optimised': 136 HTML pages outside docs/ and archive/ (verify_site's own audited set is 144); canonical link on 102 of the 136; og:image and JSON-LD on 11 - every one of them in read/, none anywhere else; 50 root+site+guides pages checked for head copy - 0 missing titles, 0 missing or sub-60-character descriptions, four pages sharing the title 'Moved' (the redirect stubs); sitemap.xml 101 URLs with 0 <lastmod> and 0 <priority>/<changefreq>; feed.xml 9 entries; robots.txt disallows /docs/ and /sessions/ and declares the sitemap; check_all_links reports 190 pages, 241 distinct external URLs and 0 errors. Every one of those is a one-line command in sessions/0b2ffabd/repo-review.md, so a polish pass can be verified, not admired.
how_to_choose: Answer the eight rows of the decision-readiness table that are yours - most of them are one word - on the review console (decision-queue.html) or site/decisions.html. The export is the record a build session implements from.

Order matters: Q12/DP-C first (it picks the surface the design pass runs on - and it is the same question as the late review's runbook item 2, so answer it once), then SUG-14/SUG-12 (the look), then DP-B (the cadence), then SUG-13 (the measurement) once Q15 is answered. SUG-11 is unblocked except for the two-writer sitemap ownership note.
Accepting a path changes nothing on this page by itself; that is the point of the gate. An unblocked path is one green-build away after a decision is recorded.
Blocked items stay visibly blocked (Q1, Q4, Q6-family). The site shows a gap rather than filling it with a guess - and the gap is the argument that the numbers it does print are real.
